features.name: share_comments_however_pivot
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments use the word "however" as a discourse pivot, shifting from a concession or prior point to a contrasting point?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of counter-argument comments. For each comment, decide whether the commenter's own text uses "however" (case-insensitive) as a discourse pivot, i.e. a contrastive transition turning from a prior point/concession to a contrasting one. Do not count non-pivot uses (e.g. "however much", "however you define it"), or "however" appearing only inside a quotation of someone else's text that the commenter does not adopt. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements or outcome reports as evidence. Output = number of qualifying comments / total number of comments, in [0,1]. Empty list gives null; missing or malformed input gives null.

h0: share_comments_however_pivot has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Higher share_comments_however_pivot is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view.
note: "More persuasive" operationalised as the dataset outcome delta (OP changed view); an association, not causal. Row-level share of comments is used since per-comment outcomes are unavailable; rows with no comments get null. Comments are current text; timing is unknown, and comment text may contain outcome announcements, which the prompt excludes as evidence. The OLS is a linear probability model.
